title: Financial Freedom of Filipinos in Personal Finance Management
tldr: Filipinos face financial literacy challenges rooted in cultural tendencies like come-what-may attitude and reliance on traditional saving methods, hindering effective budgeting and investment.
problem_and_motivation: Many Filipinos lack financial literacy and awareness of financial instruments, resulting in poor cash management, high debt reliance, and insufficient emergency funds.
approach: Descriptive methodology with linear regression analysis using 150 respondents from ten corporations on the Philippine Stock Exchange Index.
Examines four personal finance dimensions: cash management, debt management, risk management, and wealth management.
Evaluates impact of these dimensions on achieving financial independence.
findings: Pervasive financial literacy challenges rooted in cultural come-what-may attitude.
Reliance on traditional saving methods (alkansya) hinders effective budgeting and investment.
Low levels of emergency fund preparedness and high debt reliance among Filipinos.
Structured financial planning enhances wealth accumulation and mitigates financial stress.
Tailored financial education programs needed for working parents and young professionals.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides empirical evidence of financial literacy challenges among Filipino working professionals. Identifies cultural attitudes as barriers to effective personal finance management. Highlights the need for tailored financial education programs.
directly_justifies: Cultural come-what-may attitude hinders effective financial planning.
Traditional saving methods limit investment and wealth accumulation.
Structured financial planning enhances wealth and reduces financial stress.
limits: Sample from ten companies on PSE Index limits generalizability.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 domains. Flagged 1.B, 1.C, 2.A, 7.A, 13.A (high), 2.D (medium). Rejected algorithmic topics (4.B-6.B, 8.A-14.C) as this is a survey-based behavioral study.

limitations: Sample from ten PSE Index companies may not represent all Filipino workers.
Descriptive design limits ability to establish causality.
Self-reported data may introduce response bias.
